confidence_notes: I checked current prices with three web searches. Two cost-of-living sites, Numbeo (April 2026) and Wise, agree on cappuccino at about USD 3.50, a mid-range meal for two at about USD 60, and an inexpensive meal at about USD 25. HikersBay is much lower for the inexpensive meal, at about USD 10, so I used USD 20 as a blended figure. Draft beer is USD 6.00 on Numbeo but ARS 4,926 on Expatistan (May 2026), which would be lower in dollars, so I estimated USD 5. The cocktail is based on one Expatistan downtown-club figure (ARS 14,900), converted with an assumed exchange rate of roughly ARS 1,400-1,500 per USD and adjusted down slightly for a typical bar. I found no price for a glass of wine, so I estimated it from the beer price and Argentina's cheap local wine. Argentine peso inflation and exchange-rate swings make every USD figure for July 2026 less certain. The accommodation prices are my own estimates from general knowledge, not from searches or booking sites. They assume Ushuaia is a remote, expensive tourist town and that July is ski season at Cerro Castor, when demand is moderate.
comparable_city_reasoning: I compared Ushuaia with other Patagonian tourist towns such as El Calafate and Bariloche. All three charge more than Buenos Aires for drinks and accommodation because they are remote and heavily touristed. Expatistan's figures suggest Ushuaia's overall cost of living is close to Buenos Aires.
